title: Building and evaluating AI Agents — Sayash Kapoor, AI Snake Oil
talk_summary: Kapoor argues agents fail because evaluation is hard, static benchmarks mislead, and capability is confused with reliability; he recommends cost-aware, real-workflow evals and human-edited criteria. He frames AI engineering as reliability engineering for stochastic components, warning that imperfect verifiers can make retry/best-of-N worse.

takeaways.what_they_do: They evaluate agents on a Pareto frontier of accuracy and dollar cost per task, so a cheaper model with similar score is preferred.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you can have multiple agents which are evaluated with cost alongside accuracy
takeaways.numbers: Claude $57 vs o1 $664 on CORE-Bench; inference cost dropped >2 orders of magnitude since 2022

takeaways.what_they_do: They distinguish best-of-k capability from consistent pass^k reliability and argue deployed agents need repeated success, not occasional success.
takeaways.evidence_quote: reliability means consistently getting the answer right each and every single time
takeaways.numbers: 90% to 99.999% reliability gap; 80% success called catastrophic for a product

takeaways.what_they_do: They show unit tests and LLM judges can pass wrong outputs; false positives make retry/best-of-N curves bend downward.
takeaways.evidence_quote: verifiers can also be imperfect in practice
takeaways.numbers: HumanEval and MBPP have false positives; no exact count given

takeaways.what_they_do: Domain experts proactively edit the criteria used by LLM judges, rather than relying on fixed static metrics.
takeaways.evidence_quote: humans in the loop who are domain experts who proactively edit the criteria

takeaways.what_they_do: They test agents on actual tasks in a production-like workflow over time instead of trusting static benchmark scores.
takeaways.evidence_quote: over a month of use they tried it for 20 different tasks and it was only successful at three of them

takeaways.what_they_do: They treat agent systems as reliability engineering: design software abstractions around stochastic LLM calls rather than assuming model quality alone fixes failures.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it's a system design problem rather than just a modeling problem
